summary.plain: In its first 60 live days of running, LZ saw data consistent with background only: no sign of dark matter. The paper sets new limits on how strongly a WIMP (a hypothesised dark matter particle) could scatter off ordinary matter; the most stringent, at a WIMP mass of 36 GeV/c², rejects cross sections above 9.2×10⁻⁴⁸ cm² at 90% confidence.
summary.technical: SR1: 60 live days, 5.5 t fiducial, 23 Dec 2021 - 11 May 2022. Data consistent with background only; spin-independent WIMP-nucleon cross sections above 9.2 × 10⁻⁴⁸ cm² rejected at 90% CL at 36 GeV/c², with limits also set on spin-dependent WIMP-neutron and WIMP-proton couplings for WIMP masses above 9 GeV/c².

title: First Dark Matter Search Results from the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) Experiment
why_it_matters: This was LZ's first WIMP search (60 live days, 5.5 t fiducial mass); its most stringent limit is for spin-independent scattering at 36 GeV/c². In SURF's announcement of the result, LZ researchers reported that with the initial run 'LZ is already the world's most sensitive dark matter detector'.
